questions.question: What is the name of your EP2 professor
choices: (e) Wait... isn't it a chemistry quiz???
questions.explanation: Professor Yurii Maravin teaches the EP2 course.

questions.question: There is a long wire with a length of 1,000,000,000 m. The current flowing through the wire is 0 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the distance of 1 m from the wire?
choices: (c) It depends on the direction of the current
questions.explanation: With zero current (I = 0), the magnetic field $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = 0$ T regardless of wire length or distance.

questions.question: When applying the right-hand rule, what is often the best extremity to employ?
questions.explanation: The right-hand rule uses your right hand to determine directions in magnetism.

questions.question: The needle of a good compass points due north in Kansas. Where would it point in Australia?
choices: (e) Nowhere, compasses do not work down-under
questions.explanation: A compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field lines, pointing toward the north magnetic pole regardless of hemisphere location.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines are
choices: (a) ... like electric field lines - they start at north pole and terminate at south pole
(b) ... unlike electric field lines - they form closed loops that pass through north and south pole
questions.answer: (b) ... unlike electric field lines - they form closed loops that pass through north and south pole
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines always form closed loops because magnetic monopoles do not exist. Electric field lines start and end on charges.

questions.question: Which current-carrying wire configuration would produce a magnetic field pattern most similar to that produced by the earth?
questions.explanation: Earth's magnetic field resembles a dipole field like that of a bar magnet or solenoid.

questions.question: The photo below shows the coil for a DC motor like the one you built in studio. The coil's copper wire is coated with insulation that has to be removed in a particular way to establish a commutator, so that the motor works correctly. What should be done?
choices: (b) The insulation should be removed completely from both sides
(c) The insulation should be completely removed on the left side, but left completely intact on the right side
(d) The top half of the insulation should be removed from the left side and the bottom half has to be removed from the right side
(e) The top half of the insulation should be removed from the left side and all the insulation has to be removed from the right side
questions.answer: (e) The top half of the insulation should be removed from the left side and all the insulation has to be removed from the right side
questions.explanation: This creates a commutator that allows current to flow only when the coil is in the correct orientation for continuous rotation.

questions.question: Which direction will the force produced by the field from the lower wire act on the rectangular current carrying loop?
questions.explanation: The wire and loop carry parallel currents (same direction), which attract each other via magnetic force.

questions.question: Suppose you stood directly underneath high voltage DC power lines carrying current towards the south. Which way would the magnetic field produced by these wires point at your position?
questions.explanation: Using right-hand rule: thumb points south (current direction), fingers curl around wire. Directly below the wire, field points east.

questions.question: Electrons are going around a circle in a counterclockwise direction as shown. At the center of the circle they produce a magnetic field that is:
questions.explanation: Electrons moving counterclockwise create a current in the clockwise direction (opposite). Using right-hand rule for clockwise current loop: field points into page at center.

questions.question: Which graph shown below correctly gives the magnitude of the magnetic field outside an infinitely long, very thin, straight current-carrying wire as a function of the distance r from the wire?
questions.explanation: For a long straight wire: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, which gives a 1/r relationship (hyperbolic decay). Graph V shows this behavior.

questions.question: The magnetic field at the center of the solenoid has a magnitude
questions.explanation: For solenoid: $B = \mu_0 n I$. From image, approximately 15 turns over 20 cm gives $n = 75\,\text{turns/m}$. With $I = 10$ A: $B = (4\pi \times 10^{-7})(75)(10) \approx 9.4 \times 10^{-4}$ T.

questions.question: The bar magnet to the left of the solenoid in the picture above will be
questions.explanation: Current creates solenoid with left end as S pole. Bar magnet's N pole (left) is attracted to solenoid's S pole, pulling it right.

questions.question: The magnitude of the magnetic field at point P at the center of the semicircle shown is given by
questions.explanation: A full circle produces $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$ at center. A semicircle produces half: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4R}$.

questions.question: A piece of aluminum develops a small magnetic field pointing away from the north pole of the bar magnet when the bar magnet is brought close. The field goes away when the bar magnet is removed. Aluminum is
questions.explanation: Paramagnetic materials develop temporary magnetization aligned with external field but lose it when field is removed.

questions.question: A piece of unknown material is strongly attracted to a bar magnet and retains magnetization when the bar is removed. The unknown material should have an appreciable amount of
questions.explanation: Materials that retain magnetization are ferromagnetic. Iron is the classic ferromagnetic element.

questions.question:
Here is a concept for an electromagnetic projectile launcher sometimes called a rail gun. The rail gun consists of a battery supplying a voltage V₀ when switched into the circuit. Two very small resistance parallel conducting rails connect to the battery. The circuit is completed by a bar of length L, mass m, and resistance R that can slide along the rails; the bar serves as the projectile. A magnet produces a field of magnitude B₀ that exerts a force on a sliding bar. Suppose the rails are oriented vertically with the horizontal sliding bar positioned in an east-west direction, and the current in the bar moving towards east when the circuit is connected.
(a) (3 points) Which direction does the B-field need to point for an upward vertical force to develop on the projectile?
(b) (6 points) Show that the magnitude of the force on the bar just after the circuit is connected, in terms of V₀, R, B₀, and L, is F = V₀B₀L/R.
(c) (3 points) Take V₀ = 100 V, B₀ = 0.1 T, L = 10 cm, R = 0.1 Ω, and m = 10 g and determine the acceleration experienced by the bar.
questions.answer: See answer key PDF for detailed solution.

questions.question:
Suppose we wish to make an 20 cm long solenoid with a cross-sectional area of 10 cm². We have available a 100 m long roll of wire characterized by a resistance-per-length dR/dL = 0.005 Ω/m. To operate safely, the solenoid cannot dissipate more than Pmax = 100 W through the heating of its coil. If we used all the available wire and operated the solenoid with I = 10 A of current, then:
(a) (4 points) Show that the solenoid will have about N = 892 total turns
(b) (6 points) What would the field be at the center of the solenoid?
(c) (4 points) Determine whether the coil is operating safely with this current.
